reason: the correctness lens's findings the code or a test must fix

findings.text: correctness lens, high: `current_iter` is written only after an iteration *completes* (line 2803), so for a run interrupted mid-iter 2 after iter 1 completed, the real on-disk value is 1, not 2; the resume formula `_start_iter = current_iter = 1` re-runs iter 1 instead of resuming iter 2, breaking DSITER-1 and DSCMBR-1 for every N>1 interruption. (core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:2378; fix: code)

correctness lens, medium: The fixture calls `zb_engine_loop_state rounds=2` to produce `current_iter=2`, but a real engine interrupted during iter 2 produces `current_iter=1` (the write for iter 2 never fires on a mid-iter abort); the test validates the resume formula against an impossible state and will pass whatever the code does, so it cannot detect the off-by-one described above. (tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh:51; fix: test)

correctness lens, medium: Same artificial fixture is used for the DSCMBR-1 scenario ('iter 2 interrupted'): `zb_engine_loop_state rounds=2` writes `current_iter=2`, but the real engine leaves `current_iter=1` after a mid-iter-2 interruption, so the test for member-skip in the interrupted iteration exercises a state the engine never actually produces. (tests/integration/resume-loop-state-test.sh:211; fix: test)

correctness lens, medium: The `parallel:*` and `map:*` arms of the dispatch-unit loop have no resume-mode skip guard and no `skip_until_stage` guard; a complete parallel or map group is re-dispatched on resume, and groups preceding the `--from-stage` target are not skipped. (core/pipeline/runner.sh; fix: code)
